subject: Post-demo: DPA responsibility matrix & evidence checklist
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@medicahealth.com>, Alice Moreno <alice@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 16:10:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: DPA responsibility matrix & evidence checklist

Hi Samir / Alice,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the outstanding privacy/DPA items so we can move the procurement thread forward. Action items I took away: 

1) Controller vs Processor mapping — you indicated MedicaHealth will be the Controller for customer data. Please confirm that stays the requirement across the pilot and production.

2) Subprocessors — you asked for a written list of subprocessors and any tiers (cloud infra, managed services). We can provide our current list and commit to 30-day notification for new subprocessors; confirm whether you need executed subprocessor agreements.

3) Breach notification SLA — you asked about timing. Our standard is to notify customer within 72 hours for incidents that meet breach criteria; for high-severity incidents we notify as soon as reasonably possible. Please confirm whether MedicaHealth requires a shorter window (24 hours) or additional reporting fields.

4) Data residency and logs — you mentioned logs retained for audit / security for at least 1 year in your environment. Our default hosted retention for request logs is 90 days; we offer extended retention for dedicated and private deployments. Can you confirm the retention window you require for the pilot? Also specify region requirement (US only or EU/US hybrid).

5) Evidence pack — SOC2 Type II, encryption in transit & at rest summary, KMS integration, penetration testing cadence. Please confirm the exact artifacts you need to kick off procurement.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Draft_v1.pdf (DPA draft), DPA_Response_Template.xlsx (blank responsibility matrix you can fill).

Next steps I propose: you share the completed responsibility matrix (or markups to the DPA) and any minimum legal/technical must-haves by end of week; I will loop in legal and our solutions engineer to produce the subprocessors list and the evidence pack.

Best,
Markus
Sales Lead, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@medicahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Moreno <alice@medicahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: DPA responsibility matrix & evidence checklist

Markus — thanks for the clear summary and for the materials. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: MedicaHealth will be the Controller. We expect Redwood to act as Processor for hosted and dedicated deployments. Please note we may ask for limited controller-like responsibilities in scenarios where Redwood performs enrichment or looks at customer-provided labels — we will call that out if so.

- Subprocessors: we require a current subprocessor list that names the provider and function (e.g., compute: AWS us-east-1; monitoring: Datadog). A 30-day notice is reasonable; however, for any new subprocessor that stores or processes PII we require written confirmation and an executed subprocessor addendum.

- Breach notify: our security team prefers 24 hours for incidents that materially impact PII. If you cannot meet 24 hours for hosted customers, please confirm 72 hours plus immediate preliminary notification for critical incidents.

- Logs/Retention: For our pilot we need token-level request logs and error traces retained for 180 days; for full production we will require 1 year. Are those retention levels feasible for dedicated and hosted? Can you provide sample log schema and redaction rules (what we get vs. what is masked)?

- Compliance artifacts: At minimum we need SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summary, and encryption-at-rest proof (KMS). For HIPAA use cases we will require a BAA — is Redwood able to sign a BAA or support a customer-hosted private deployment that allows us to control keys?

I attached a redline of your DPA with our initial comments (MedicaHealth_DPA_redline_v1.docx). Please route the redline to your legal team; in parallel, can you provide a populated responsibility matrix for the items above?

Thanks — we’d like to keep procurement moving this week.

—Samir
Director, Product Security
MedicaHealth
[Attachment: MedicaHealth_DPA_redline_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@medicahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: DPA responsibility matrix & evidence checklist

Markus / Monica / Samir — thanks for the thread and the redline. High-level legal guidance and suggested reply below.

1) Controller/Processor: Confirmed — MedicaHealth is Controller; Redwood will act as Processor for hosted and Dedicated offerings. For Private deployments where MedicaHealth manages the environment and keys, Redwood remains the software vendor but can be treated operationally as a Processor acting under customer direction. We will reflect this in the responsibility matrix.

2) Subprocessors: We will provide a current subprocessor list with function and region. Redwood policy: 30 days' notice for new subprocessors and right to object; for subprocessors that store PII we will execute a subprocessor addendum. We cannot accept retroactive approval vetoes that block critical infra providers but can agree to remediation steps and timely notification.

3) Breach notification: Our standard obligation is to notify customers within 72 hours for incidents that meet breach criteria, with immediate preliminary notification for critical incidents impacting PII. If MedicaHealth requires contractual 24-hour notification, we can escalate to Sales/Legal to evaluate case-by-case for this customer (possible for Dedicated or Private with additional terms). Suggested compromise wording: 72-hour contract baseline + commitment to immediate preliminary notification for critical incidents and deviate to 24 hours under negotiated SLA for Dedicated/Private customers.

4) Logs & retention: Default hosted retention is 90 days. We can extend to 180 days for pilot (fee may apply) and 1 year for production on Dedicated/Private. We will provide sample log schema and a redaction/PII-masking description. For customers requiring KMS or customer-managed keys, we can support Private deployments or Dedicated with CMK options — Ops will confirm feasibility and cost.

5) BAA / HIPAA: Redwood can sign a BAA under Private or Dedicated deployment models where we can meet required technical and administrative controls. For hosted customers we need a legal review and potential restrictions; please confirm the scope of PHI processing before we commit.

Actionables: 
- Markus: send the attached responsibility matrix (populated) with the proposed compromises (subprocessor notice, 72h baseline + immediate prelim, retention options).
- Monica / Ops: prepare subprocessors list and a sample log schema + redaction note.
- Samir: please confirm whether you want us to aim for a negotiated 24-hour breach SLA for Dedicated/Private, and confirm the minimum log retention you need for the pilot (Samir indicated 180 days).

I’ll draft the legal-friendly language for the response DPA redline and attach a clean responsibility matrix for discussion.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
